summary.text: List 3 of River's Spelling Bee study words: thimble, custody, granola, warrior, rigid, fierce, laughter, salary, disappear, hurdler, lounge, jovial.

why.text: This is the real Scripps "Two Bee" fourth-grade word list — the words a school spelling bee actually draws from. Saying each word aloud, letter by letter, is the same skill a real bee tests, not just recognizing the word on a page.

objectives.text: Spell every word on this list correctly, letter by letter, from hearing it alone.
State each word's meaning in your own words.

parentNote.text: Built from "Spelling Bee Words", the 2026-27 Scripps Two Bee fourth-grade study list you added to her Drive folder. All 50 official words are split across four lessons; every definition and example sentence here was written fresh, since the source is a bare word list with no definitions to copy. The flashcards use the honeycomb "bee" look, and each lesson also opens the Spelling Bee voice game — hear it, spell it aloud letter by letter.

nextUp.text: Cards first to learn the meanings, then the Spelling Bee game to practice saying the letters aloud.

cards.def:
**A small protective cap, usually metal, worn on the finger to push a needle while sewing.**
• Grandma always kept a silver thimble in her sewing box.
cards.hint: THIM- + -BLE, starting with the same TH as "thumb" — where it goes.

cards.def:
**The legal right and responsibility to care for and protect someone, or the state of being guarded.**
• After the divorce, the parents shared custody of their two children.

**A breakfast and snack food made of rolled oats mixed with nuts, dried fruit, and a sweetener, often baked crisp.**
• She packed a bag of granola for the hike.

**A person who fights in battles, especially one known for courage or skill; a brave fighter.**
• Ancient stories often describe a lone warrior defending the village.

**Stiff and unable to bend, or — for a rule or person — very strict and unwilling to change.**
• The metal rod stayed perfectly rigid even under heavy weight.

**Showing intense, powerful energy or aggression; wild and forceful.**
• A fierce wind bent the young trees nearly to the ground.

**The action or sound of laughing, usually in response to something funny or joyful.**
• Laughter filled the room as the puppy chased its own tail.
cards.hint: LAUGH (the GH sounds like an F) + -TER.

cards.def:
**A fixed amount of money paid regularly, usually monthly or yearly, for doing a job.**
• Her new salary let her start saving for college.

**To stop being visible; to vanish from sight completely.**
• The rabbit seemed to disappear into the tall grass.
cards.hint: DIS- + APPEAR — one S in "dis", double P in "appear".

cards.def:
**An athlete who runs and jumps over a series of barriers, called hurdles, in a race.**
• The hurdler cleared every barrier without knocking one down.

**A comfortable room for sitting and relaxing, or the act of sitting or lying back in a relaxed way.**
• They chose to lounge by the pool instead of hiking that afternoon.
cards.hint: LOUNGE rhymes with "sponge" — the E keeps the G soft.

cards.def:
**Cheerful, friendly, and full of good humor.**
• The jovial shopkeeper greeted every customer with a joke.
cards.hint: JOVI- (from Jove, another name for the god linked to good fortune) + -AL.

questions.q: Spell the word: a small protective cap, usually metal, worn on the finger to push a needle while sewing.
questions.hint: THIM- + -BLE, starting with the same TH as "thumb" — where it goes.

ex.tip: A thimble protects the thumb or finger — both words share that TH start.

questions.q: Spell the word: the legal right and responsibility to care for and protect someone, or the state of being guarded.

ex.tip: "Custom" and "custody" share their first four letters exactly.

questions.q: Spell the word: a breakfast and snack food made of rolled oats mixed with nuts, dried fruit, and a sweetener, often baked crisp.

ex.tip: It starts like "grain" — the food it is mostly made from.

questions.q: Spell the word: a person who fights in battles, especially one known for courage or skill; a brave fighter.
steps: Double the R, then add I-O-R.

ex.tip: It starts with the whole word "war" — the fighting it describes.

questions.q: Spell the word: stiff and unable to bend, or — for a rule or person — very strict and unwilling to change.

ex.tip: The G sounds soft, like a J, but it is still spelled with a plain G.

questions.q: Spell the word: showing intense, powerful energy or aggression; wild and forceful.
steps: F, then I before E: F-I-E.
Finish with R-C-E — the soft C sound needs that final E.

ex.tip: Rhymes exactly with "pierce" — same I-E-R-C-E ending.

questions.q: Spell the word: the action or sound of laughing, usually in response to something funny or joyful.
questions.hint: LAUGH (the GH sounds like an F) + -TER.
steps: L-A-U-G-H — the GH makes an F sound.

ex.tip: "Laugh" keeps its silent-looking GH even inside a longer word.

questions.q: Spell the word: a fixed amount of money paid regularly, usually monthly or yearly, for doing a job.

ex.tip: Only one L, even though the first syllable is stressed hard.

questions.q: Spell the word: to stop being visible; to vanish from sight completely.
questions.hint: DIS- + APPEAR — one S in "dis", double P in "appear".

ex.tip: The prefix DIS- has one S; the double letter is the P inside "appear".

questions.q: Spell the word: an athlete who runs and jumps over a series of barriers, called hurdles, in a race.

ex.tip: It is "hurdle" plus one letter, R, at the very end.

questions.q: Spell the word: a comfortable room for sitting and relaxing, or the act of sitting or lying back in a relaxed way.
questions.hint: LOUNGE rhymes with "sponge" — the E keeps the G soft.
steps: Add a final E to keep the G sound soft.

ex.tip: Without the E, "loung" would look like it should end hard — the E is what makes it say "-nj".

questions.q: Spell the word: cheerful, friendly, and full of good humor.
questions.hint: JOVI- (from Jove, another name for the god linked to good fortune) + -AL.

ex.tip: Named after Jove/Jupiter — old astrologers thought that planet brought good cheer.
